text: Core positioning: The research focuses on "enterprise full life cycle management," covering the entire process from establishment and daily operation to strategic upgrading. It not pays attention only to the optimal allocation of resources such as "people, finance, materials, and information," but also emphasizes the dynamic adaptation of enterprises to external environments such as markets, policies, and technologies. Ultimately, it aims to maximize organizational efficiency. Significant features: Comprehensiveness: Integrates knowledge from multiple fields such as management, economics, psychology, and sociology—for example, using economics to analyze market laws and psychology to understand employee behavior—emphasizing a cross-disciplinary perspective. Practicality: Oriented toward solving practical problems, it transforms theory into operational management methods through case analysis, simulation training, and enterprise practice. Broad adaptability: Not applies only to industrial and commercial enterprises but also covers management scenarios in various organizations, such as government departments and non-profit organizations, making it highly universal.
